chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, raising it, said:

It was said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Some people claim that the waxing (of the head/body) on Friday is disliked.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is not where they are going. Which cleanliness is more cleansing than the waxing on Friday?'

key_terms.النُّورَةَ: Grooming, specifically removing hair from the body and head

ai.seo_question: Is removing hair or grooming on Friday considered disliked in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) refutes the claim that grooming (removing hair) on Friday is disliked, asserting instead that it is a superior form of ritual cleanliness (tahur). This hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on physical and spiritual preparation for the congregational prayer, framing personal hygiene as an act of worship that enhances the sanctity of the day.
